Subject: Hosted API pricing — request for higher per-token lift and commit structure

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Helio is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the built-in caching — we think this will materially reduce inference cost for our product. We're preparing a Q3 commit and I wanted to get a candid read on whether Redwood can support a ~40% off list per-token band at scale, or an equivalent committed-discount structure.

Quick context: our engineering forecast (attached) shows peak sustained usage of ~2.0B tokens/month starting July, with monthly spikes to ~2.8B for training-related workloads. We're comfortable committing to a 12-month hosted usage agreement if we can get predictable unit economics.

Ask: outline two options we can take to procurement today — (A) a straight per-token custom rate at volume X (list rate is attached), (B) a commit tier (monthly committed spend) with step-down banding and a usage true-up. We also need any required SLA language or separate contract addenda to enable the discount.

Attached: Helio_Projected_Volume_Q3.xlsx, Helio_Request_Summary.pdf

Would love to know the internal approval path and what you need from our side (PO, payment terms, legal redlines).

Best,
Maria Torres
CFO, Helio Labs

Hi Maria — great to hear and thanks for the detailed forecast. We appreciate the scale and the clarity on the commitment window.

Short answer: we can propose both paths, but a 40% flat off-list will likely require an approved exception (commercial/finance signoff) because it sits well below our published ratecard. The standard route that often works for large usage is a committed spend with milestone breakpoints + performance SLAs; that lets us protect margin while giving you predictable unit cost.

I'm happy to draft two concrete proposals for your review:
- Proposal A: Custom per-token band (one negotiated effective rate starting at 1.5B tokens/month, true-up monthly, 30-day payment terms).
- Proposal B: 12-month committed spend ($X/month baseline) with tiered per-token step-downs at 1B / 1.8B / 2.5B thresholds, and a usage true-up. Includes standard hosted SLA and optional dedicated burst pool for peak windows.

Before I escalate internally, can you confirm target effective per-token you need (in $/1k tokens or $/M tokens) and whether you're willing to include a minimum monthly commitment? That will speed approvals.

I'll include the redwood_ratecard_v2.pdf and pull in Finance/Commercial as needed.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Helio's ask. Summary:
- Helio forecasts ~2.0B tokens/month (spikes to ~2.8B) starting July; willing to do 12-month commit.
- They are asking for ~40% off list per-token OR commit tier that yields similar effective rate.
- They need clarity on SLA and contract addenda.

My read: Helio is strategic (large usage, fast growth). Per our standard tolerance, discounts >30% require commercial committee and finance signoff; 40% is outside playbook unless we structure a commit with non-trivial monthly minimum and tighter payment terms (net 15) + termination penalties. I think a middle path: approve a provisional tiered commit with an effective ~28-32% discount at the 2B+/month level, with a performance corridor and a rollback to list if usage drops below 60% of forecast for two consecutive months.

Specific asks I have for you:
- Karthik: can you run margin sensitivity on (A) straight 40% off list vs (B) 12-month commit with $X baseline and step-downs? Include GPU cost assumptions and KV cache impact.
- Marissa: do we have precedent for the termination/true-up language that Finance will accept for a monthly usage true-up? Also, any FYI on legal redlines for dedicated burst addenda?

They want an expedite — target response to Helio by Fri.

Thanks,
Grace

Thanks for the context, Grace. I'm comfortable with a conditional approval path but want guardrails. Proposed internal decision:
1) Approve Proposal B (12-month committed spend with tiered step-downs) as the principal commercial path. No flat 40% off-list without a minimum guaranteed ARR of $X (finance to confirm exact threshold).
2) Approve a max effective discount cap of 33% at the highest tier (>=2.5B tokens/mo) with the following conditions:
   - Minimum monthly commitment equal to 70% of forecasted tokens converted to dollars.
   - Payment terms Net 15 for the first 3 months, then Net 30 after verified performance.
   - Usage true-up monthly with a clawback if usage <60% of committed baseline for two consecutive months.
   - Addendum for dedicated burst pool subject to infra capacity planning and on-call SLO.
3) Karthik/Finance: return a margin sensitivity and suggested $X ARR threshold by EOD Thu so we can share a concrete number with Helio Friday AM.

If everyone is aligned, Grace: please send the conditional Proposal B draft to Helio and mark it as "subject to finance sign-off". Keep legal looped for the addendum language. I want commercial to avoid precedent creep — if we approve >33% for Helio today, we'll see similar asks across top 10 accounts.
